title: Quantum Risk Observatory
subtitle: From a correlated derivatives book to the quantum estimation oracle.

cases.label: Base market
cases.title: The portfolio, under pressure.
cases.description: Four correlated option positions. Revalue the full book at a 21-day horizon and compare three simulation designs at matched path budgets.
method: Correlated GBM terminal simulation; Black–Scholes revaluation of remaining six-month option maturities. Positions and currency scale are explicit.
Randomized Sobol and antithetic designs are compared with independent Monte Carlo using 12 separate seeds at four budgets. The high-budget independent reference is itself a simulation estimate.
VaR is an empirical loss quantile; expected shortfall averages observations in the empirical tail. PFE uses positive future book value, not losses.
limitations: Illustrative synthetic asset parameters, not calibrated market data or an investment recommendation.
Lognormal dynamics omit stochastic volatility, defaults, liquidity and funding; tail estimates remain model dependent.
The chart compares mean-loss error. It does not establish quantum advantage or tail-quantile confidence intervals.

cases.label: Quantum oracle
cases.title: Look inside the quantum estimator.
cases.description: An eight-scenario register and a payoff ancilla, explicit unitary preparation, amplitude amplification and maximum-likelihood estimation.
method: Prepare amplitudes sqrt(p_j(1-f_j)) and sqrt(p_j f_j) on the scenario/ancilla basis. Householder state preparation is unitary and explicitly inverted inside the Grover operator.

A Bernoulli likelihood over Grover powers estimates the bounded expectation. The profile-likelihood bounding interval is 0.24740 to 0.25293; it is an asymptotic, potentially disconnected likelihood set.
At the same 8960 preparation-query budget a recorded direct Bernoulli estimate is 0.24967. One random trial is not a comparative performance study.
limitations: Dense unitary simulation is exponential and is not a compiled fault-tolerant implementation.
This bounded discrete payoff is separate from the portfolio's unbounded continuous loss; no claim that the oracle directly estimates its VaR is made.
State preparation, inverse preparation and Grover queries are counted. Device gates, errors, compilation and classical inference costs are not hidden in a speedup claim.

cases.label: Calibrated scenarios
cases.title: How much does calibration change this book?
cases.description: As of 2025-12-31; closes 2025-01-13 to 2025-12-31. Generated synthetic price CSV; no market observations. Same positions, strikes, horizon and normal shocks across three parameter sets.

charts.title: 99% risk metrics under frozen and fitted parameters

method: CSV assets are mapped by names A, B, C, D. Cutoff excludes later prices; at least 60 complete rows are required. Full parameter snapshots and input SHA-256 are included in the exported study.
Annual covariance = 252 times sample covariance of log returns (ddof=1); 90% sample plus 10% its diagonal. This fixed shrinkage is a design choice, not an estimated optimal shrinkage coefficient.

Spot-matched baseline uses CSV final spots with frozen volatilities and correlations. Its difference from calibrated scenarios isolates the joint volatility/correlation change, including repricing the initial book.
All models use the same Sobol normal draws. Frozen assumptions are labeled 2025-12-31; their date is illustrative, not a historical market snapshot.
Calibrated minus spot-matched VAR: mean -89.2971 USD across 12 independent scrambles (seeds 100–111); numerical standard error 0.5908 USD.
Calibrated minus spot-matched ES: mean -103.3021 USD across 12 independent scrambles (seeds 100–111); numerical standard error 0.0936 USD.
Calibrated minus spot-matched PFE: mean -32.0035 USD across 12 independent scrambles (seeds 100–111); numerical standard error 0.2711 USD.
limitations: Historical close-to-close covariance is used as a constant scenario and pricing volatility proxy; it is not an implied volatility surface.
The drift remains the fixed 3% rate, not an estimated physical expected return. These are model scenarios, not validated real-world tail probabilities.
252 equal trading steps per year are assumed; supply consecutive synchronized adjusted daily closes. No holiday, split or dividend adjustment is inferred.
Gaussian GBM discards skewness, heavy tails and volatility clustering, even when present in the input CSV. Calibration does not validate this model.
Twelve scramble changes measure numerical variability only; parameter uncertainty and out-of-sample accuracy are unmeasured.

cases.label: Non-Gaussian model risk
cases.title: What changes when variance is random?
cases.description: As of 2025-12-31. Generated synthetic price CSV; no market observations. Fixed fitted parameters and pricing rule; a two-state common variance changes the return distribution.

charts.title: 99% tail risk at the displayed shared seed
Mixture minus GBM across twelve shared seeds

method: Fit the same CSV covariance and spots as the calibration case. Hold all contracts, horizon, initial value and Black-Scholes repricing inputs fixed across models.

Independently draw a common variance V: 4 with probability 0.1, otherwise 2/3. E[V]=1; centered standardized innovations have kurtosis 6 versus Gaussian 3. These parameters are specified, not estimated.
Use conditional GBM drift r - V sigma squared / 2 and shocks sqrt(V) L Z. Expected terminal spots match GBM. The shared state also changes joint tail dependence.
Use plain Monte Carlo and exactly the same normal draws within each pair. A separate SeedSequence branch supplies independent regime uniforms. Display seed 1729; replicates 100 through 111.

VaR is the interpolated empirical 99% loss quantile; ES is the mean at or above it. PFE uses positive undiscounted future value. The GBM row uses Monte Carlo and need not equal the calibration case's Sobol row.
Mixture minus GBM VAR: paired mean 26.5503 USD; numerical SE of the mean 1.5666 USD across twelve seeds.
Mixture minus GBM ES: paired mean 81.2760 USD; numerical SE of the mean 2.0373 USD across twelve seeds.
Comparison cost: 851,968 book paths and 3,407,872 future option valuations; excludes RNG, fitting, runtime and quantum costs.
limitations: The variance states and 10% probability are specified sensitivity assumptions, not fitted or selected by held-out performance. Input covariance alone does not identify tail shape.

E[V]=1 matches innovation covariance; random conditional drift adds a small term to log-return covariance. Conditional drift preserves expected terminal spots. This is a finite Gaussian mixture, not a power-law tail model.
One common variance state persists over the entire horizon; there is no time evolution, transition estimation, leverage effect or volatility-clustering validation.
Black-Scholes repricing volatility stays fixed in both models, isolating scenario sensitivity; this is not consistent mixture-model option pricing or a fitted volatility surface.

Twelve paired seed differences describe numerical variability only, not parameter uncertainty, tail coverage, market accuracy or out-of-sample validation. The 3% drift is illustrative, not fitted physical drift.
Synthetic bundled prices; no real-world accuracy or quantum advantage is established. Portfolio tail risk remains separate from the bounded quantum oracle.

comparison.data_source: Generated synthetic price CSV; no market observations
comparison.method: plain Monte Carlo with common normal draws across models

model_specification.name: Two-state common horizon variance mixture
model_specification.terminal_formula: S_h = S_0 exp((r - V sigma^2/2) h + sigma sqrt(h V) L Z)
model_specification.pricing_rule: Fixed fitted-volatility Black-Scholes for both initial and future book values

comparison.seed_protocol: Normal draws: default_rng(seed).standard_normal((paths, 4)); independent regime uniforms: default_rng(SeedSequence(seed, spawn_key=(3103,))).random(paths). Same normals across models; one V shared by all assets in a path.
